lesson_title: Cutting the Loaf: Ratio, Rate and Proportion
hook_text: Two bags of maize meal. One is cheaper. Your eyes cannot tell you which — but one division can.
clip_script: Two bags on the shelf. 2,5 kilograms for R42,99. Ten kilograms for R159,99. Which one is actually cheaper? Your eyes are useless here, because the bags are different sizes. So do what granny does — get both down to ONE kilogram. R42,99 shared over 2,5 kilograms: about R17,20 a kilogram. R159,99 shared over ten: R16,00 a kilogram. The big bag wins, by about R1,20 every single kilogram. That's around twelve rand back in your pocket. And it's the same move everywhere. Bakkie does 480 kilometres on 40 litres? Twelve kilometres per litre. Water at R14,50 a kilolitre, you used 18? R261. Price of ONE, times how many. Now the grown-up part: cheaper per kilogram is only better if you HAVE the R159,99 today, and if the meal gets eaten before the weevils find it. Say the number — then say the condition. That's a complete answer, and complete answers get the tick.
visual_style: A supermarket aisle at eye level: two maize-meal bags, price tags glowing, then both dissolving into a single one-kilogram scoop with a rand figure above it; quick cuts to a bakkie fuel gauge and a water meter counting kilolitres.
mood: Warm, streetwise, quietly triumphant — the confidence of someone who never gets overcharged.
pacing: Slow curious open on the two bags, brisk middle through the divisions, calm settled close on the condition.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never guess at a shelf price again.
